markdown_report:
Select the endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff treatment against the now-documented uniform control. At 30% progress, this isolates a feasible sampling intervention before introducing architectural changes.

Three insights from the supplied experiment guide this choice. First, measured training already uses equal, separately normalized reconstruction and terminal losses. Establishing that objective again would repeat the control rather than test recency.

Second, Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific have weaker tenth-percentile training margins, 0.5434 and 0.624. This motivates investigating terminal discrimination, although these measurements neither isolate terminal examples nor establish validation performance.

Third, only 15.9–27.7% of eligible users have histories where the proposed sampling policies differ. Consequently, aggregate effects may be small, and exposure accounting is essential.

Three literature insights define the alternatives. BERT4Rec [1] establishes masked reconstruction and appended-mask prediction; RSS [2] motivates revisiting target sampling. Together they support a modest adaptation, with limited novelty.

TiSASRec [3] distinguishes elapsed time from sequence position. Its temporal mechanism motivates a later BERT4Rec attention experiment, but requires careful handling of unavailable future timestamps.

MARS [4] motivates composing finer item attributes. Its pretrained encoders and richer attributes limit transfer to an encoder trained from scratch using only supplied text.

The framework separates **target exposure**, **temporal context**, and **item specificity**, while retaining one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category. Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Recent nonterminal cutoff mixture [1,2] | 2/7/7/6/3 | Originality: precise contrast, established ingredients. Potential: reusable control, limited affected population. User: targets stale and broad matches, cannot infer fulfilled needs. Model: changes terminal exposure, weaker margins are not terminal-specific. Difficulty: local sampler edit, exact accounting needs care. |
| Historical-gap attention bias [3] | 4/7/7/5/6 | Originality: BERT adaptation, established temporal mechanism. Potential: learns persistence, risks suppressing useful history. User: targets stale and diffuse interests, proximity is imperfect. Model: contextual differentiation, geometry supplies no causal evidence. Difficulty: small parameter addition, predictor/interface changes are substantial. |
| Joint title-token embedding [4] | 3/6/6/5/7 | Originality: constrained composition, familiar architecture. Potential: sparse-item transfer, weak text supervision. User: finer matches, compatibility remains uncertain. Model: shared statistical strength, no measured text-specific failure. Difficulty: ordinary token pooling, vocabulary and scoring integration add work. |

For the selected experiment, keep endpoint probability 0.1 and change only conditional nonterminal sampling to half uniform and half uniform over the latest ten eligible positions. This explicitly targets older-interest dominance and broad associations displacing current-purpose matches; improved lower-tail discrimination is a model-facing hypothesis. It cannot establish whether purchases satisfied a need.

Retain strict-prefix MASK targets, equal branch losses, matched seeds, and unchanged inference. Compare using pinned macro validation HR@10; the supplied 0.5975 is a control selection summary, not paired treatment evidence. Resolve diagnostic definitions mentioning 0.25/0.75 against the recorded 0.5/0.5 protocol before interpreting allocation. Track full-catalog judgments separately for the same twenty users.

idea.description: Test only the conditional nonterminal cutoff distribution in the established equal-loss BERT4Rec control: retain endpoint probability 0.1 and replace uniform nonterminal selection with an equal mixture of uniform selection and uniform selection among the latest ten eligible nonterminal event positions. Train one independent model per category and deploy one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The supplied uniform-control records make the next sampling comparison concrete. Recent-prefix supervision could reduce older-interest dominance and broad associations that displace specific current-purpose recommendations, addressing two explicit user failures. Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific have comparatively weak lower-tail sampled training margins, motivating a terminal-discrimination experiment. These margins pool supervised positions and do not prove terminal-specific weakness, representation collapse, or expected validation gains. Only approximately 21.1%, 15.9%, 16.7%, and 27.7% of eligible users, respectively, have histories where the policies can differ; this limits the intervention's reach.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate the sampler below into the supplied corrected baseline; baseline source was not provided, so this is an integration component rather than an invented replacement train.py. The existing uniform control is documented, although a fresh matched control may be necessary if its exact executable configuration and selection records cannot be reproduced. Never load its trained checkpoint into the treatment or combine predictions.

Preserve the documented configuration: 64 reconstruction and 64 terminal examples per update, independent user draws, 0.15 MASK-only reconstruction with one-target fallback, tied real-item-only full-softmax output weights, no output bias, Adam learning rate 0.001, and all other baseline settings. Compute loss as 0.5 times reconstruction target-mean CE plus 0.5 times terminal target-mean CE. Changing the loss weights, output denominator, user distribution, or reconstruction corruption would confound this sampling comparison.

For target event index t, retain only history[max(0,t-(maxlen-1)):t], append reserved MASK, and left-pad. Never expose the target occurrence or later events. Earlier occurrences of the same item remain permissible history. Histories with fewer than two events are ineligible; length-two histories select their sole eligible endpoint. For longer histories, endpoint probability remains exactly 0.1. Policies coincide when the number of nonterminal targets is at most ten. Position recency does not imply elapsed-time recency, fulfilled demand, or compatibility.

Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Preserve the documented SeedSequence streams, category order, one-based epochs and zero-based batches. Keep model initialization and dropout separate from data RNG. Run exactly 200 batches per executed epoch and cap resolved SASREC_EPOCHS at 200. Retain baseline validation cadence, stopping rule and earliest-checkpoint tie handling. Select through the unchanged pinned host macro validation HR@10; report all four category outcomes. Do not treat historical 0.5850 scores or the supplied 0.5975 category-selection summary as paired evidence of improvement.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], the supplied splits and four dataset routes, single-GPU execution, and trial-local artifacts. All training, diagnostics and failures count against 43,200 GPU seconds. Do not inspect other trials, hidden test files, or additional datasets. Deploy exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint per category, without averaging or fitted auxiliary scores.

Preserve appended-mask inference and the matching embedded predictor writer. Read features at the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1. Architecture and checkpoint tensor shapes need no change for this sampler intervention. Preserve family-specific sample_batch, actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and all ModelView data interfaces.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Existing definitions refer to a 0.25/0.75 experiment while recorded protocols report 0.5/0.5; generate definitions from the checkpoint's resolved configuration and report missing information as unavailable. Persist selected-checkpoint training counters rather than inferring allocation from unmatched diagnostic batches. Distinguish full-history endpoint selections from targets located at a presented sequence's final position.

Record expected and realized endpoint selections, affected-history exposure, target frequencies, context lengths, branch target counts, target-weighted CE, and timing. Measure terminal margins with a separately identified strict-prefix diagnostic sample; retain reconstruction probes for comparison. Sampling changes jointly alter target frequencies and context lengths, so the experiment estimates the total policy effect rather than a pure recency mechanism.

Use only supplied histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. For the same twenty real training users, separately track current willingness to choose, stale or broad matches, duplication and compatibility rejection, and uncertain identification. Treat these judgments as qualitative follow-up, not replacements for host validation. If aligned host per-user hits are available, report gained/lost hits and an exploratory paired within-category bootstrap; otherwise omit uncertainty estimates requiring unavailable outcomes.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

CATEGORIES = (
    'Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
    'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl',
)

def data_rng(category_id, one_based_epoch, zero_based_batch, purpose_id):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, one_based_epoch, zero_based_batch, purpose_id]))

def choose_target(history, uniform, treatment=True):
    """Return zero-based target index and explicit sampling status."""
    n = len(history)
    if n < 2:
        return None, 'ineligible'
    if not 0.0 <= uniform < 1.0:
        raise ValueError('uniform must lie in [0, 1)')
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    if uniform < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    v = (uniform - 0.1) / 0.9
    m = n - 2
    probabilities = np.full(m, 1.0 / m, dtype=np.float64)
    if treatment:
        k = min(10, m)
        probabilities *= 0.5
        probabilities[-k:] += 0.5 / k
    cdf = probabilities.cumsum()
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    j = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1)
    return j + 1, 'nonterminal'

def terminal_example(history, uniform, maxlen, mask_id, treatment=True):
    if maxlen < 2:
        raise ValueError('maxlen must reserve context and MASK positions')
    t, status = choose_target(history, uniform, treatment)
    if t is None:
        raise ValueError('sample only eligible training histories')
    context = list(history[max(0, t - (maxlen - 1)):t])
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    tokens = context + [mask_id]
    sequence[-len(tokens):] = tokens
    positive = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    positive[-1] = history[t]
    return sequence, positive, t, status

# Integration into the unchanged corrected baseline:
# Each epoch: exactly 200 updates, maximum 200 epochs.
# Keep 64 baseline reconstruction examples and 64 terminal examples.
# Generate users/cutoffs/corruption with purpose IDs 0/1/2.
# Construct terminal examples using treatment=True; control uses False.
# R = summed valid reconstruction CE / reconstruction target count.
# T = summed valid terminal CE / terminal target count.
# Raise if either target count is zero.
# loss = 0.5 * R + 0.5 * T; update the single BERT4Rec network.
# Persist counts/configuration with that category's selected checkpoint.
# Inference remains left_pad(history[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK]).
# Read maximum nonpadding index and score real items with the same model.

originality.positive: Fixing endpoint exposure and all objective details makes the sampling-policy contrast precise and falsifiable.
originality.negative: BERT4Rec already uses terminal masking, and recency-weighted sampling has prior work; this is an experimental refinement.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive foundation for later elapsed-time or context-length-controlled experiments while directly testing current-interest sensitivity.
future_potential.negative: Most eligible histories receive unchanged sampling probabilities, and event recency cannot identify fulfilled demand or physical compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The principal change is confined to cutoff sampling and requires no architecture or inference modification.
code_difficulty.negative: Matched random streams, checkpoint-aligned counters, and correction of inconsistent diagnostic definitions require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item training and appended-mask next-item inference.
Provides the backbone and terminal-supervision precedent for the proposed experiment.
limitations: Interior reconstruction can use right context unavailable during terminal prediction.
Does not establish that this cutoff mixture improves the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Recency-sampling research (RSS; supplied source)
contributions: Motivates examining target sampling and the alignment between reconstruction and next-item prediction.
limitations: Substantially limits novelty of recency-weighted target exposure.
Does not validate the proposed fixed-endpoint mixture under this host protocol.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models historical time intervals alongside sequence positions.
Motivates a separately budgeted temporal-attention adaptation within BERT4Rec.
limitations: Its backbone and evaluation differ from this constrained BERT4Rec experiment.
Terminal prediction requires a convention that never uses an unknown future timestamp.

related_work.title: MARS (2024; supplied attribute-aware recommendation source)
contributions: Motivates multiple attribute-aware representations and finer item matching.
limitations: Uses pretrained language representations and richer structured attributes unavailable here.
Does not establish effectiveness of title and description representations trained entirely from scratch.
